summary: Liu and Wang compute topological cyclic homology of the ring of integers O_K of every finite extension K/Q_p with F_p coefficients, including p = 2. They descend along 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z], z ↦ ϖ_K: THH, TC⁻ and TP of O_K relative to 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n] are known from BMS2 (Theorem 2.17), and TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is determined as a δ-ring inside a Nygaard-completed PD envelope (Theorem 1.3, using an HKR theorem for HP of lci quotients, Theorem A.1). The resulting descent spectral sequences have E^2 given by comodule Ext over Hopf algebroids, i.e. coherent cohomology of a stack 𝒳 conjecturally equal to WCart_{O_K}; E^2(THH) recovers Lindenstrauss–Madsen, and a refinement of the Nygaard filtration indexed by (1/e_K)Z makes all differentials of the 'refined algebraic Tate spectral sequence' computable by hand (Proposition 6.43). Analysing can and φ on the mod p E^2-pages gives E^2(TC(O_K); F_p) with classes β, λ, γ, α^{(j)}_{i,l} and its collapse (Theorem 8.18), hence TC_*(O_K; F_p) for p odd (Theorem 8.20, as in Hesselholt–Madsen), for p = 2 (Theorem 8.21, new for ramified K by this route), d = [K(ζ_p):K] (Proposition 8.23) and a TC-level Lichtenbaum–Quillen statement (Remark 1.8). In the atlas, KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 plans the classical odd-p calculation and keeps its p = 2 caveat, and the method is planned nowhere, so the paper's own theory becomes a Part II of KTheoryFiniteLocalFields; the general trace-method inputs go as sources to RefinedTraceMethods RT.6 (§2) and RT.1 (Appendix A), and L.5 is recorded as planning Corollary 5.19 and Theorem 8.20. Fourteen misprints and one error in a proof (a congruence mod p that holds only mod ζ_p − 1, Proposition 8.23) are recorded; no stated result is affected.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 / 8.18: the E^2-page of the mod p descent spectral sequence for TC(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let d = [K(ζ_p):K]. There are explicitly constructed classes β ∈ E^2_{0,2d}(TC(O_K); F_p), λ ∈ E^2_{−1,0}, γ ∈ E^2_{−1,2d+2} and α^{(j)}_{i,l} ∈ E^2_{−1,2j} (1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K) such that, as F_p[β]-modules, E^2_{0,*} = F_p[β], E^2_{−1,*} = F_p[β]{λ, γ} ⊕ F_p[β]{α^{(j)}_{i,l}}, E^2_{−2,*} = F_p[β]{λγ}, and E^2_{i,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, −1, −2; E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−2,*} are concentrated in even degrees. Consequently the descent spectral sequence converging to TC_*(O_K; F_p) collapses at E^2.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, arXiv v4 p. 5; Theorem 8.18 and Corollary 8.19, arXiv v4 p. 57
items.note: The main theorem, valid for every p and every K, including p = 2. Assembled from Propositions 8.11, 8.12, 8.14, 8.15, Corollary 6.15 and the multiplicativity of the mod p E^2-pages (Remark 6.1). The identification of d with [K(ζ_p):K] is Proposition 8.23 (item 004).

items.name: Theorem 8.20: TC_*(O_K; F_p) for p odd
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let p be odd and d = [K(ζ_p):K]. Then TC_*(O_K; F_p) ≅ F_p[β]{1, λ, γ, λγ} ⊕ F_p[β]{α^{(j)}_{i,l} : 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K} as F_p[β]-modules, with |β| = 2d, |λ| = −1, |γ| = 2d + 1, |α^{(j)}_{i,l}| = 2j − 1; in particular it is a free F_p[β]-module.
items.locator: Theorem 8.20, arXiv v4 p. 57
items.note: KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 plans 'the calculation of THH/TR/TC for … the complete DVRs required for local-field K-theory' (Hesselholt–Madsen's route through log de Rham–Witt). Liu–Wang reprove it from Theorem 8.18 (item 001): for p odd the Moore spectrum is multiplicative, so there are no hidden extensions.

items.name: Theorem 8.21: TC_*(O_K; F_2)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let p = 2 (so d = 1), with the Bott class β ∈ TC_2(O_K; F_2) and the Z_2[β^4]-module structure from the v_1^4 self-map of 𝕊/2. As Z_2[β^4]-modules, TC_*(O_K; F_2) is isomorphic to F_2[β^2]{1} ⊕ Z/4[β^2]{β} ⊕ F_2[β]{λ, γ} ⊕ F_2[β^2]{βλγ} ⊕ F_2[β]{α_{i,l} : 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K} if [K:Q_2] is odd, and to F_2[β]{1, λ, γ, λγ} ⊕ F_2[β]{α_{i,l}} if [K:Q_2] is even; |β| = 2, |λ| = −1, |γ| = 3, |α_{i,l}| = 1. Equivalently, the 2-extension of β^k is nontrivial exactly when k is odd and [K:Q_2] is odd; this happens iff Hamilton's quaternions do not split over K.
items.locator: Theorem 8.21 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 58–59; Remark 8.22, arXiv v4 p. 59
items.note: New for ramified K/Q_2 by this method (previously known through Mitchell's 2-adic K-theory and Rognes–Weibel). L.5 keeps the p = 2 hypotheses 'until a separately proved theorem removes them'. Proof: the 2-extension of β^k is k c̄²β^{k−1}, with c detecting ∂(β)/2 = η; its triviality reduces to whether x² − x = 1 splits over k. The printed degree |α_i| = 2i − 1 is a misprint (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 8.23: d = [K(ζ_p):K]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let d be the least positive integer with p − 1 | e_K d and N_{k/F_p}(μ̄)^d = 1. Then d = [K(ζ_p):K].
items.locator: Proposition 8.23 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 59–60
items.note: Uses μ = p/N_{K/K_0}(−ϖ_K) and, for d' | d, reduction to a tame, then totally tamely ramified with p − 1 = e_K d_1, then μ = 1 situation, where K(ϖ_K^{1/d_1}) = K_0(ζ_p) by Hensel's lemma. One congruence in the proof is misstated (recorded under sourceIssues). Remark 8.25: the proof uses E_K(0) ≡ p mod p², the normalization forced by Theorem 2.15(4).

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen for O_K via TC
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. TC(O_K; F_p) → L_{K(1)}TC(O_K; F_p) ≃ TC(O_K; F_p)[β^{−1}] is 0-truncated; consequently TC(O_K; Z_p) → L_{K(1)}TC(O_K; Z_p) and K(O_K; Z_p) → L_{K(1)}K(O_K; Z_p) are 0-truncated. After base change to K(ζ_p), β is, up to a scalar and higher filtration, the d-th power of the Bott element, and the Bott element is detected by β; d = 1 iff ζ_p ∈ K.
items.locator: Remark 1.8, arXiv v4 p. 6; Remark 8.24, arXiv v4 p. 60
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 8.18 in remarks, with the Bott element identification sketched. MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 and KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.6 plan the K-theoretic statement by the motivic/étale route; the TC-level statement and its derivation from the descent spectral sequence are not planned.

items.name: Relative topological Hochschild homology THH(A/E)
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring E and an E_∞-E-algebra A, THH(A/E) = A^{⊗_E 𝕋} (the tensor with the circle in E_∞-E-algebras), the universal 𝕋-equivariant E_∞-E-algebra with a nonequivariant map from A; THH(A) = THH(A/𝕊). It is multiplicative: THH(A_1/E_1) ⊗_{THH(A_2/E_2)} THH(A_3/E_3) ≃ THH(A_1 ⊗_{A_2} A_3 / E_1 ⊗_{E_2} E_3).
items.locator: Definition 2.1 and (2.2), arXiv v4 p. 8
items.note: RT.2 constructs THH of E_1-algebras with its circle action; the relative version over an E_∞ base is THH in E-modules. HH = THH(−/Z) is not cyclotomic (Nikolaus–Scholze III.1.10).

items.name: Lemma 2.3: cyclotomic structures on relative THH
items.statement: (1) Let E be an E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra with trivial underlying 𝕋-action. A lift of the augmentation THH(E) → E to a map of E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra determines a lift of THH(−/E) to a functor to E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra, via THH(X/E) ≃ THH(X) ⊗_{THH(E)} E. (2) For a commutative square of such lifts for E_1 → E_2 extending to E_∞-maps E_1 → A_1, E_2 → A_2, the induced map THH(A_1/E_1) → THH(A_2/E_2) is a map of E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3, arXiv v4 p. 9
items.note: Essentially BMS2 Construction 11.5, which the BMS2 extraction routes to RT.6 (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/107).

items.name: TC^-, TP and TC relative to a cyclotomic base; the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: When Lemma 2.3(1) applies, TC^-(−/E) = THH(−/E)^{h𝕋}, TP(−/E) = THH(−/E)^{t𝕋}, with Frobenii φ_l : THH(−/E) → THH(−/E)^{tC_l} and can : TC^- → (THH^{tC_l})^{h𝕋}, and TC(−/E) = fib(Π_l(φ_l^{h𝕋} − can)). After p-completion TP(−/E; Z_p) ≃ (THH(−/E)^{tC_p})^{h𝕋} and TC(−/E; Z_p) = fib(φ − can : TC^-(−/E; Z_p) → TP(−/E; Z_p)). There are the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences THH_*(−/E)[v] ⇒ TC^-_* and THH_*(−/E)[σ^{±1}] ⇒ TP_* (|v| = (−2, 0), |σ| = (2, 0), can(v) = σ^{−1}); the Nygaard filtration 𝒩^{≥j} on TP_* is the abutment filtration E^∞_{*,j}, multiplicative, with projections p_j : 𝒩^{≥j}TP_0 → THH_j when the Tate spectral sequence collapses.
items.locator: Definition 2.4 and (2.5)–(2.9), arXiv v4 pp. 10–11
items.note: RT.2: 'Construct TC, TC⁻ and TP with their comparison maps'; Nikolaus–Scholze Lemma II.4.2 for TP ≃ (THH^{tC_p})^{h𝕋}.

items.name: Proposition 2.10: cyclotomic structures on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}) and THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])
items.statement: There are functorial E_∞-cyclotomic structures on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}) (using the E_∞-Frobenius of 𝕊_{W(k)}, which agrees with the p-completed cyclotomic structure of THH(𝕊_{W(k)}) via the augmentation) and on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) (using 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] ≃ 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] with BMS2's cyclotomic structure on 𝕊[z], trivial 𝕋-action and Frobenius z ↦ z^p). THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ THH(O_K)^∧_p and THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) ≃ THH(O_K/𝕊[z])^∧_p, and likewise for TC, TC^- and TP.
items.locator: Proposition 2.10, Convention 2.11 and Remarks 2.12–2.13, arXiv v4 p. 11
items.note: The BMS2 extraction routes the cyclotomic structure on THH relative to 𝕊[z] to RT.6.

items.name: Proposition 2.14: the Frobenius on the image of z
items.statement: Under i_C : 𝕊[z]^{h𝕋} → TC^-_0(−/𝕊[z]; Z_p) and i_P : (𝕊[z]^{tC_p})^{h𝕋} → TP_0(−/𝕊[z]; Z_p), the cyclotomic Frobenius satisfies φ(z) = z^p (i.e. φ(z) = can(z)^p).
items.locator: Proposition 2.14, arXiv v4 p. 11

items.name: Theorem 2.15 (Bökstedt, Nikolaus–Scholze): TP and TC^- of F_p
items.statement: THH_*(k) = k[u] with u ∈ THH_2(k) the Bökstedt element. (1) The Tate spectral sequence for TP_*(F_p) and the homotopy fixed point spectral sequence for TC^-_*(F_p) collapse; TP_*(F_p) = TP_0(F_p)[σ^{±1}] and can : TC^-_j(F_p) → TP_j(F_p) is an isomorphism for j ≤ 0. (2) TP_0(F_p) = Z_p, p_0 is Z_p → F_p, and φ is the identity on TC^-_0(F_p) ≅ TP_0(F_p). (3) For every lift u_{F_p} ∈ TC^-_2(F_p) of the Bökstedt element there is a unique v_{F_p} ∈ TC^-_{−2}(F_p) with TC^-_*(F_p) = TC^-_0(F_p)[u, v]/(uv − p). (4) φ(u_{F_p}) = can(v_{F_p})^{−1}.
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.15, arXiv v4 p. 12
items.note: Cited from Nikolaus–Scholze Corollary IV.4.16. As in the BMS2 extraction, Bökstedt periodicity is planned in L.5 ('THH/TR/TC for perfect fields').

items.name: Theorem 2.17(1)–(5): THH, TC^- and TP of O_K relative to 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. (1) THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) = O_K[u] for any lift u of the Bökstedt element. (2) The Tate spectral sequence for TP_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) collapses and TP_* = TP_0[σ^{±1}], |σ| = 2. (3) TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) = W(k)[[z]], with p_0 the W(k)-algebra map z ↦ ϖ_K. (4) The homotopy fixed point spectral sequence collapses, can induces TC^-_j ≅ 𝒩^{≥j}TP_j for all j, and can is an isomorphism for j ≤ 0. (5) The Frobenius φ : TC^-_0 → TP_0 is the Frobenius of W(k) with z ↦ z^p.
items.locator: Theorem 2.17(1)–(5) and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 12–14
items.note: From BMS2 Proposition 11.10 by Proposition 2.10's completions; the BMS2 extraction routes that proposition to RT.6 (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/109).

items.name: Theorem 2.17(6): the normalization uv = E_K(z) with E_K(0) = p
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For any u_{F_p} as in Theorem 2.15 there are unique u ∈ TC^-_2(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) lifting u_{F_p}, v ∈ TC^-_{−2} and σ ∈ TP_2 with φ(u) = σ, can(v) = σ^{−1}, TP_* = TP_0[σ^{±1}] and TC^-_* = TC^-_0[u, v]/(uv − E_K(z)), where E_K is normalized by E_K(0) = p. Consequently the Nygaard filtration on TP_0 = W(k)[[z]] is 𝒩^{≥2j} = 𝒩^{≥2j−1} = (E_K(z))^j for j ≥ 0.
items.locator: Definition 2.16, Theorem 2.17(6) and proof, Convention 2.19, arXiv v4 pp. 12–14; Remark 8.25, arXiv v4 p. 60
items.note: BMS2's argument gives uv = λ(z)E_K(z) for a unit λ; comparing with F_p via z ↦ 0 and Theorem 2.15 shows λ(0) = 1, and a unit b with λ = φ(b)/b rescales (u, v, σ). Remark 8.25: this normalization agreeing with E_K(0) = p is equivalent to Theorem 2.15(4). The printed proof mixes primed and tilded symbols (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 3.1: the cyclotomic structure on THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Regard O_K as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]-algebra via z_0, z_1 ↦ ϖ_K (and as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]-algebra via all z_i ↦ ϖ_K). THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) ≃ THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0]) ⊗_{THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)})} THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_1]) has a natural structure of E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra; the maps z ↦ z_0, z ↦ z_1 give left and right units η_L, η_R.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 and the paragraph after it, arXiv v4 p. 14

items.name: Divided power envelopes, their Nygaard (PD) filtration, and divided power algebras
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and an ideal I, D_R(I) is the divided power envelope of I in R, filtered by 𝒩^{≥2j}D_R(I) = 𝒩^{≥2j−1}D_R(I) = the R-span of the divided powers I^{[l]}, l ≥ j, and D_R(I)^∧_𝒩 is its completion; Γ_A(M) is the divided power algebra of an A-module M, graded with M in degree 2. For W(k)[z_0, z_1] and the regular sequence (E_K(z_0), z_0 − z_1), D is generated over W(k)[z_0, z_1] by the E_K(z_0)^{[i]}(z_0 − z_1)^{[j]}.
items.locator: §3, statement of Theorem 3.2 and §1, arXiv v4 p. 15; Appendix A, arXiv v4 p. 62
items.note: CR.0 plans PD envelopes over a PD base with explicit envelopes for polynomial regular immersions and PD filtrations. Mathlib has the DividedPowers structure (Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowers/Basic.lean:78) and the free divided power algebra DividedPowerAlgebra (Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean:100, as a quotient ring, without its divided power structure), but not envelopes.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 / A.1: Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg for periodic cyclic homology of lci quotients
items.statement: Let R be a commutative Z_p-algebra, I ⊂ R a locally complete intersection ideal and A = R/I, with R I-adically separated and A p-torsion-free. Then HP_0(A/R) is canonically isomorphic, as a filtered ring, to the completion of the divided power envelope D_R(I) with respect to its Nygaard filtration (𝒩^{≥2j}D_R(I) = 𝒩^{≥2j−1}D_R(I) the R-span of the I^{[l]}, l ≥ j); the Tate spectral sequence for HP(A/R) collapses at E^2; and HH_*(A/R) ≅ Γ_A(I/I²) as graded rings.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2, arXiv v4 p. 15; Appendix A, Theorem A.1 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 62–64
items.note: Proof via the Koszul dga R[x]/(x²), dx = a, and Connes' double complex for a principal ideal; tensor products for a regular sequence; Zariski descent in general. Remark 3.3: also obtainable from BMS2's motivic filtration on HP and Bhatt's derived de Rham computation for lci maps.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.6: THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) up to associated graded
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Regard O_K as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]-algebra via z_0, z_1 ↦ ϖ_K (and as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]-algebra via all z_i ↦ ϖ_K). Let t_{z_0−z_1} ∈ THH_2(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) = HH_2(O_K/W(k)[z_0, z_1]) ≅ I/I² be the class of z_0 − z_1. The graded ring associated with the u_0-adic filtration of THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is O_K[u_0] ⊗_{O_K} O_K⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩; hence THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is a p-torsion-free integral domain concentrated in even degrees.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.6, arXiv v4 pp. 15–16
items.note: THH(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])/u_0 ≃ THH(O_K/O_K[z_1]) = HH(O_K/O_K[z]) = O_K⟨t⟩, and the u_0-Bockstein spectral sequence collapses.

items.name: Corollary 3.7 and Remark 3.8: degeneration for 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Lemma 3.14: Frobenius divisibility from the Nygaard filtration

items.name: The (p, 𝒩)-topology
items.statement: For a ring R with a multiplicative decreasing filtration 𝒩^{≥•}, the 𝒩-topology is the filtration topology, and the (p, 𝒩)-topology has basis of neighbourhoods of 0 the (p^j) + 𝒩^{≥j}, j ≥ 0. Neither is adic in general. TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) is complete and separated for both, and its Frobenius is continuous for the (p, 𝒩)- but not the 𝒩-topology.
items.locator: Definition 3.16 and Remark 3.17, arXiv v4 p. 17

items.name: δ-rings
items.statement: A δ-ring is a commutative ring R with a map of sets δ : R → R, δ(0) = δ(1) = 0, δ(xy) = xδ(y) + yδ(x) + pδ(x)δ(y) and δ(x + y) = δ(x) + δ(y) + (x^p + y^p − (x + y)^p)/p. For p-torsion-free R this is the same as a Frobenius lift φ, via δ(x) = (φ(x) − x^p)/p.
items.locator: §1 and Definition 3.20, arXiv v4 p. 18

items.name: Proposition 3.23: the elements h, δ^k(h) and f^{(k)}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. By Lemma 3.14 there is h ∈ TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) with hφ(E_K(z_0)) = φ(z_0 − z_1) = z_0^p − z_1^p. Define δ^{k+1}(h) = (φ(δ^k(h)) − δ^k(h)^p)/p and f^{(0)} = z_0 − z_1, f^{(k+1)} = (−(f^{(k)})^p + δ^k(h)E_K(z_0)^{p^{k+1}})/p. items.name: Proposition 3.29: TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is a δ-ring
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Corollary 3.30 and Lemma 3.31: HP of O_K over W(k)[z] and W(k)[z_0, z_1]

items.name: Hopf algebroids as cogroupoid objects; filtered and graded freeness
items.statement: A Hopf algebroid in a symmetric monoidal category with colimits is a cosimplicial commutative algebra A : Δ → CAlg such that for every partition [n] = S ∪ S' with S ∩ S' = {s} the map A^S ⊗_{A^{{s}}} A^{S'} → A^{[n]} is an equivalence; it is written (A^{[0]}, A^{[1]}), with coproduct Δ, counit ε and conjugation c. For a complete nonnegatively filtered ring R, a complete filtered R-module M is free and locally finite if there are m_i with only finitely many outside each 𝒩^{≥j} and ⊕Rx_i → M an isomorphism after completion; similarly for graded modules over a nonnegatively graded ring. M is free and locally finite iff Gr(M) is, and completed tensor products of such modules are such, with Gr(M_1 ⊗̂ M_2) = Gr(M_1) ⊗ Gr(M_2).
items.locator: §4, (4.1), Definitions 4.2–4.3, Convention 4.10, arXiv v4 pp. 22–24

Both η_L and η_R exhibit TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) as a free and locally finite filtered TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])-module, and THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) as a free and locally finite graded THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])-module; in particular both are completely flat.

items.name: Lemma 4.8 and Corollary 4.9: the Hopf algebroids of THH_* and TP_0
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For 0 ≤ i ≤ n the maps THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_i]) ⊗_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_i])} THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_i, …, z_n]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) and TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_i]) ⊗̂_{TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_i])} TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z_i, …, z_n]) → TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) are isomorphisms (all over 𝕊_{W(k)}). Hence THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) and TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) are Hopf algebroids in graded rings and in complete filtered rings respectively.

items.name: Lemma 4.11 and Corollary 4.12: THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) exactly

items.name: Proposition 4.15: the Hopf algebroid structure of THH_*
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 5.9: descent along 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). The 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]-Adams resolution 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•} induces an augmented cosimplicial E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) → THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}), and THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}); likewise TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) and TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}). items.note: Uses Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Nilpotence and descent, Proposition 2.14 (the fibre of the n-th partial totalization is the (n+1)-fold smash power of the 0-connected fibre of THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) → THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])); for TP, homotopy orbits commute with finite limits and the connectivity passes through. The descent along 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] was suggested by Hesselholt.

items.name: The descent spectral sequences for THH, TC^-, TP and TC of O_K
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). The coskeleton filtrations of Proposition 5.5 give multiplicative second-quadrant spectral sequences E^1_{i,j} = THH_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[−i]}) ⇒ THH_{i+j}(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}), and likewise for TC^- and TP. By Lemma 4.8 and Corollary 4.5, E^1 is the cobar complex of the Hopf algebroid (THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]), THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])), resp. row by row of (TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]), TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])), so E^2_{i,j}(THH) = Ext^{−i,j}_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) and E^2_{i,j}(TP) = Ext^{−i}_{TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z])) (comodule Ext). Setting TC(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)})_{(n)} = fib(can − φ : lim_{Δ^{≤n}} TC^- → lim_{Δ^{≤n−1}} TP) gives the descent spectral sequence for TC, whose E^1 is the total complex of E^1(TC^-) → E^1(TP), with an auxiliary spectral sequence Ẽ^2_{i,k,j} ⇒ E^2_{i−k,j}(TC), Ẽ^2_{i,0,j} = ker(can − φ) and Ẽ^2_{i,1,j} = coker(can − φ) on E^2. Geometrically, E^2_{i,j}(TP) = H^{j−i}(𝒳, 𝒪_𝒳(j/2)) for the stack 𝒳 = colim_{Δ^op} Spec TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}).
items.locator: §1, (1.1)–(1.2), arXiv v4 pp. 2–3, and Relation with other works, p. 8; §5, pp. 26–28
items.note: The central construction of the paper, an Adams-type spectral sequence in cyclotomic spectra. §1 conjectures that 𝒳 is the Cartier–Witt stack WCart_{O_K} of Bhatt–Lurie, and that the E^2-page agrees with that of the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze motivic spectral sequence built from a quasisyntomic perfectoid resolution; neither is proved.

items.name: Proposition 5.14: the Ext computing E^2(THH(O_K))
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let D_0 : THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) be the left-linear map with D_0(t_{z_0−z_1}) = 1 and D_0(t^{[i]}_{z_0−z_1}) = 0 for i ≠ 1. Then Ext_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) is the cohomology of THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) dz, a ↦ (D_0 ∘ η_R)(a) dz, |dz| = 2, obtained from the relative injective resolution 0 → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1]) dz → 0 given by the divided-power derivative D(t^{[i]}) = t^{[i−1]}.
items.locator: (5.10)–(5.13), Proposition 5.14 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 28–29

items.name: Corollary 5.19 (Lindenstrauss–Madsen): THH_*(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Ext^{0,0}_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) ≅ O_K, Ext^{1,2n} ≅ O_K/(nE'_K(ϖ_K)) for n ≥ 1, and all other Ext groups vanish; the descent spectral sequence for THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) collapses at E^2. Hence THH_0(O_K; Z_p) = O_K, THH_{2n−1}(O_K; Z_p) ≅ O_K/(nE'_K(ϖ_K)) for n ≥ 1, and the other groups vanish.
items.locator: Corollary 5.19 and Remark 5.20, arXiv v4 pp. 29–30
items.note: Recovers Lindenstrauss–Madsen (TAMS 2000); Krause–Nikolaus give another descent proof. L.5 plans THH of the complete DVRs needed for local-field K-theory; the proof here is a two-term Ext computation (Proposition 5.14, item 037).

items.name: The algebraic Tate and algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequences
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The Nygaard filtration on the rows of E^1(TP(O_K)) and E^1(TC^-(O_K)) gives multiplicative spectral sequences E^1_{i,j,k} = H^i(Gr^{2k} TP_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•})) ⇒ E^2_{−i,j}(TP(O_K)) (algebraic Tate) and the same with TC^- (algebraic homotopy fixed points), with d^r : E^r_{i,j,k} → E^r_{i+1,j,k+r}, one row j at a time; E^1_{i,j,k}(TP) = E^1_{−i,2k}(THH(O_K))σ^{j/2} for j even and 0 for j odd, and the algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequence is a truncation of the algebraic Tate one.
items.note: By Remark 3.8 (item 018) the Tate spectral sequences of all TP(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) collapse, so E^2(THH(O_K))[σ^{±1}] ⇒ E^2(TP(O_K)). This replaces the topological Tate differentials of earlier work by algebraic ones.

items.name: Proposition 5.23: E^2(TC^-(O_K)) and E^2(TP(O_K)) have two columns
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. E^2(TC^-(O_K)) and E^2(TP(O_K)) are concentrated in the columns E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−1,*}; hence the descent spectral sequences for TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) and TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) collapse at E^2.
items.locator: Proposition 5.23, arXiv v4 p. 30; Remark 1.7, arXiv v4 p. 5
items.note: From Corollary 5.19 through the algebraic spectral sequences. Remark 1.7: geometrically, 𝒳 has coherent cohomology in degrees 0 and 1 only.

items.name: The mod p descent spectral sequences and their multiplicativity
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). THH_*, TP_* and TC^-_* of O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} are p-torsion-free, so their mod p versions are the reductions mod p, and the coskeleton filtrations give descent spectral sequences E^1_{i,j} = THH_j(O_K/𝕊[z]^{⊗[−i]}; F_p) ⇒ THH_{i+j}(O_K; F_p), and likewise for TP, TC^- and TC (with Ẽ^2_{i,0,j} = ker(can − φ), Ẽ^2_{i,1,j} = coker(can − φ)); E^2 is comodule Ext over the mod p Hopf algebroids. Although the mod p Moore spectrum, hence THH(O_K; F_p), TC(O_K; F_p) etc., is multiplicative only for p ≠ 2, the E^1- and E^2-pages of all the mod p descent spectral sequences are multiplicative for every p.
items.locator: §6, opening paragraphs and Remark 6.1, arXiv v4 pp. 31–32
items.note: The multiplicativity for p = 2 holds because the descent spectral sequences of O_K are multiplicative and the reductions of the E^1-terms are surjective; this is what lets the method reach p = 2, where the Toda bracket ⟨2, η, 2⟩ ≠ 0 obstructs earlier approaches.

items.name: Proposition 6.2: the E^2-page of the mod p descent spectral sequence for THH(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Here THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p) = k[z]/(z^{e_K})[u]. (1) E^2_{0,*}(THH(O_K); F_p) has k-basis z^l u^n with 1 ≤ l ≤ e_K − 1 or p | e_K n if e_K > 1, and u^n with p | n if e_K = 1. (2) E^2_{−1,*} has k-basis the cycles z_1^l(u_0^{n−1}t_{z_0−z_1} − (n−1)E'_K(z_0)u_0^{n−2}t^{[2]}_{z_0−z_1}) with 0 ≤ l ≤ e_K − 2 or p | e_K n if e_K > 1, and the reductions of u^{(n)} = Σ_{j=1}^{n} ((n−1)!/(n−j)!)(−E'_K(z))^{j−1}u_0^{n−j}t^{[j]}_{z_0−z_1} = (u_0^n − u_1^n)/(nE'_K(z)) with p | n if e_K = 1. (3) E^2_{i,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, −1.
items.locator: Proposition 6.2 and proof, (6.3)–(6.6), arXiv v4 pp. 33–34
items.note: Via the two-term complex f(u) ↦ −e_K μ̄ z^{e_K−1} f'(u) dz and the comparison map u^n dz ↦ u^{(n+1)}. Remark 6.7: the 'accidental' filtration clash of z^{me_K} ↦ me_K μ̄ z^{me_K−1}dz motivates the refined Nygaard filtration. The e_K = 1 case of (2) and the orientation of the comparison square carry misprints (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: The refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Rescale Nygaard indices by 2 (𝒩^{≥j} now means the old 𝒩^{≥2j}). For a filtered TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p) = k[[z]]-module M with a Z-indexed filtration 𝒩^{≥•}, the refined filtration is indexed by (1/e_K)Z: 𝒩^{≥j+m/e_K}M = z^m 𝒩^{≥j}M + 𝒩^{≥j+1}M for j ∈ Z and 0 ≤ m < e_K. It restricts to the original filtration on Z, and it is multiplicative if 𝒩^{≥•} is (since z^{e_K} ≡ μ^{−1}E_K(z) mod p).
items.locator: Convention 6.8, Definition 6.9 and Lemma 6.10, arXiv v4 p. 34
items.note: Applied to TP_*(O_K/𝕊[z]^{⊗•}; F_p) and TC^-_* via the left unit; refining via η_L or η_R gives the same filtration since z_0^m − z_1^m ∈ 𝒩^{≥1}. The authors stress it has no topological analogue.

items.name: Lemma 6.11: the associated graded Hopf algebroid of the refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The associated graded of the refined Nygaard filtration on (TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p), TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]; F_p)) is (k[z], k[z_0] ⊗_k k⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩), with Δ(t^{[i]}) = Σ_{0≤j≤i} t^{[j]} ⊗ t^{[i−j]} and ε(t^{[i]}) = 0; if e_K = 1 then z_1 = z_0 − t_{z_0−z_1}, and if e_K > 1 then z_1 = z_0 and it is the Hopf algebra (k[z], k[z] ⊗_k k⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩).
items.locator: Lemma 6.11, arXiv v4 p. 35

items.name: The refined algebraic Tate and refined algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequences
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The refined Nygaard filtration on E^1(TP(O_K); F_p) and E^1(TC^-(O_K); F_p) gives multiplicative spectral sequences Ẽ^{1/e_K}_{i,j,k} = H^i(Gr^k TP_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}; F_p)) ⇒ E^2_{−i,j}(TP(O_K); F_p) (and the same with TC^-), with k and the page index r in (1/e_K)Z and d^r : Ẽ^r_{i,j,k} → Ẽ^r_{i+1,j,k+r}; Ẽ^{1/e_K}(TP) is the cobar complex of k[z][σ^{±1}] over the Hopf algebroid of Lemma 6.11, and Ẽ^{1/e_K}(TC^-) is a truncation of it.
items.locator: §6, paragraph after Lemma 6.11, arXiv v4 p. 35

items.name: Lemma 6.12 and Corollary 6.17: the first pages of the refined algebraic Tate spectral sequence
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. (1) If e_K > 1, Ẽ^{1−1/e_K}_{*,j,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) = k[z]σ^j ⊕ k[z_0]σ^j dz with d^{1−1/e_K}(zσ^j) = σ^j dz, where dz denotes t_{z_0−z_1}. (2) If e_K = 1, Ẽ^1_{*,j,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) = k[z^p]σ^j ⊕ z_0^{p−1}k[z_0^p]σ^j dz, where z_0^{n−1}dz denotes the cycle Σ_{j=1}^{n} ((n−1)!/(n−j)!)(−1)^{j−1} z_0^{n−j}t^{[j]}_{z_0−z_1}, formally (z_0^n − z_1^n)/n. (3) Ẽ^{1/e_K}_{i,*,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, 1.
items.locator: Lemma 6.12 and proof, Convention 6.16 and Corollary 6.17, arXiv v4 pp. 35–37
items.note: The printed statement and convention carry sign and index slips in the e_K = 1 cycle (recorded under sourceIssues); the form above is the one the proof gives.

items.name: Corollary 6.15: the mod p descent spectral sequences for TC^- and TP collapse
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. E^2(TC^-(O_K); F_p) and E^2(TP(O_K); F_p) are concentrated in E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−1,*}; hence the mod p descent spectral sequences for TC^-(O_K; F_p) and TP(O_K; F_p) collapse at E^2.
items.locator: Corollary 6.15, arXiv v4 p. 36

items.name: Lemmas 6.19–6.20: ξ_0 and the first Frobenius congruence
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let f^{(0)} = z_0 − z_1, ξ_0 = −δ(f^{(0)})/f^{(0)} and μ̃ = −μ^p/δ(E_K(z_0)). Then ξ_0 ∈ TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) and ξ_0 ≡ z_0^{p−1} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥(p−2)/e_K+1}); in particular ξ_0 ∈ (p, 𝒩^{≥(p−1)/e_K}). Moreover φ(f^{(0)}) ≡ μ̃ z_0^{pe_K+p−1} f^{(0)} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥2p}) (refined, rescaled indices).
items.locator: Lemmas 6.19–6.20 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 37–38
items.note: Uses hφ(E_K(z_0)) = φ(f^{(0)}) and f^{(1)} = δ(f^{(0)}) − hδ(E_K(z_0)) ∈ 𝒩^{≥p} from Proposition 3.23 (item 024). The proof of Lemma 6.19 has an exponent slip (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemmas 6.23, 6.28 and 6.29: Frobenius iterates of z_0 − z_1 modulo p
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. With μ̃ as above: if p > 2 and e_K > 1, then for l ≥ 1, φ^l(f^{(0)}) ≡ μ̃^{(p^l−1)/(p−1)} z_0^{(pe_K+p−1)(p^l−1)/(p−1)} f^{(0)} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥p^l(1+1/(p−1)+1/e_K)}). If p = 2, then (f^{(1)})^{2^l} ∈ (2, 𝒩^{≥2^{l+1}(1+1/4)}) for l ≥ 1, and if moreover e_K > 3, then φ^l(f^{(0)}) ≡ μ̃^{2^l−1} z_0^{(2^l−1)(2e_K+1)} f^{(0)} mod (2, 𝒩^{≥2^l(2+1/e_K)−2/e_K}).
items.locator: Lemma 6.23, Lemma 6.28 and Lemma 6.29 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 38–40
items.note: Induction on l from Lemma 6.20; the p = 2 case uses 2f^{(2)} = −(f^{(1)})² + δ²(h)E_K(z_0)^4 and δ²(h) ∈ 𝒩^{≥1} (Lemma 4.11).

items.name: Proposition 6.32: the refined algebraic Tate differentials on stem 0 (large e_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Suppose p > 2 and e_K > 1, or p = 2 and e_K > 3. For n ≥ 0, l = v_p(n) and n' = n/p^l, d^{(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)−1/e_K}(z^n) = n' μ̃̄^{(p^l−1)/(p−1)} z_0^{pe_K(p^l−1)/(p−1)+n−1} dz, nonzero in Ẽ^{(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)}_{1,0,(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)+(n−1)/e_K}; the exponents of z_0 in the targets are pairwise distinct, so these are all the nontrivial refined algebraic Tate differentials on stem 0.
items.locator: Proposition 6.32 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 40–41
items.note: From Lemmas 6.23 and 6.29 via z_0^{p^l} − z_1^{p^l} ≡ φ^l(f^{(0)}) mod p and a binomial expansion. The proof's expansion uses n where n' is meant (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 6.34 and Lemma 6.36: stem 0 for all p and e_K by tame base change
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The conclusion of Proposition 6.32 holds for every p and every K. Proof device: for m > 3 prime to p, K' = K(ϖ_K^{1/m}) has E_{K'}(z) = E_K(z^m), and z ↦ z^m induces T_m : TP(O_K/𝕊[z]^{⊗•}; F_p) → TP(O_{K'}/𝕊[z]^{⊗•}; F_p), compatible with the refined filtration of O_K and the 'less refined' ((1/e_K)Z-indexed) filtration of O_{K'}, with T_m(z^n) = z^{mn} and T_m(z_0^n dz) = m z_0^{mn+m−1} dz, injective on Ẽ^{1/e_K}_{*,0,*}; Lemma 6.36 shows that the projection of the less refined page onto the line k z_0^{pme_K(p^l−1)/(p−1)+mn−1}dz factors through the relevant later page and detects d(z^{mn}).
items.locator: Proposition 6.34, Lemma 6.36 and their proofs, Remark 6.38, arXiv v4 pp. 41–44
items.note: Remark 6.38 records the consequence used in §8: for every r, T_m is injective on the surviving classes z_0^{k−1}dz, and so (by the footnote in the proof of Proposition 8.4) on Ẽ^∞_{1,*,*}.

items.name: Lemma 6.42: survival of certain classes off stem 0
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let ε = σ_0σ_1^{−1} and ε_0 = φ(E_K(z_0))/φ(E_K(z_1)) (a unit by Remark 3.15), so ε/φ(ε) = ε_0 by Theorem 2.17(6), ε̄_0^{p^i} ≡ 1 mod 𝒩^{≥p^i} and ∏_{i≥0} ε̄_0^{p^i} = ε̄. For r ∈ (1/e_K)N, j ∈ Z and k, m ∈ N with p^k > j and min{p^m, p^k} > r, the class z^{(p^k−j)e_K(p^{m+1}−p)/(p−1)}σ^j ∈ Ẽ^{1−1/e_K}(TP(O_K); F_p) survives to Ẽ^r.
items.locator: (6.39)–(6.41), Lemma 6.42 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 44–45

items.name: Proposition 6.43: all refined algebraic Tate differentials
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For n ≥ 0 and j ∈ Z let l = v_p(n − pe_K j/(p−1)) and n' ≡ p^{−l}(n − pe_K j/(p−1)) mod p. Then d^{(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)−1/e_K}(z^n σ^j) = n' μ̃̄^{(p^l−1)/(p−1)} z_0^{pe_K(p^l−1)/(p−1)+n−1} σ^j dz, nonzero in Ẽ^{(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)}_{1,j,(p^{l+1}−1)/(p−1)+(n−1)/e_K}; the exponents of z_0 in the targets are pairwise distinct, so these are all the nontrivial refined algebraic Tate differentials.
items.locator: (6.18), arXiv v4 p. 37; Proposition 6.43 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 45–46; Remark 6.45, arXiv v4 p. 46
items.note: From Lemma 6.42 and Proposition 6.34 by the Leibniz rule. Remark 6.45 matches z, z^{e_K}, σ, dz with Hesselholt–Madsen's ϖ_K, τ_Kα_K, τ_K^{−1}, τ_Kϖ_K dlog ϖ_K (and with Rognes's and Tsalidis's classes for e_K = 1), claiming the proposition recovers their Tate differentials; the correspondence is asserted without proof. New: the case p = 2, e_K > 1.

items.name: Proposition 7.1: E^2_{0,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) and E^2_{0,*}(TC^-(O_K); F_p)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. E^2_{0,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) is nonzero iff j ≥ 0 and p − 1 | e_K j, and then it is a 1-dimensional k-vector space generated by a cycle with leading term z^{pe_K j/(p−1)}σ^j. The canonical map induces an isomorphism E^2_{0,*}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) → E^2_{0,*}(TP(O_K); F_p), with can(z^{pe_K j/(p−1)}σ^j) = μ̄^{−j}z^{e_K j/(p−1)}u^j.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1 and proof, arXiv v4 p. 47

items.name: Proposition 7.2: E^2_{−1,*}(TP(O_K); F_p)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Leading terms refer to the refined algebraic spectral sequences; write the classes of E^2_{−1,2j} by their leading terms z_0^{n−1}σ^j dz. E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) has a k-basis of cocycles with leading terms z_0^{(pe_K(j−1)+bp^l)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz for l ≥ 1 and b ∈ Z with −e_K(j−1)/p^{l−1} < b < pe_K − e_K j/p^{l−1}, p ∤ b and b ≡ −e_K(j−1) mod p − 1, together with z_0^{pe_K(j−1)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz when j > 1 and p − 1 | e_K(j−1).
items.locator: Proposition 7.2 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 47–48

items.name: Proposition 7.6: E^2_{−1,*}(TC^-(O_K); F_p)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Leading terms refer to the refined algebraic spectral sequences; write the classes of E^2_{−1,2j} by their leading terms z_0^{n−1}σ^j dz. For j ≥ 1, E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) has a k-basis of cocycles with leading terms z_0^{(pe_K(j−1)+bp^l)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz for l ≥ 0 and b ∈ Z with −e_K(j−1)/p^l < b < pe_K − e_K j/p^l, p ∤ b and b ≡ −e_K(j−1) mod p − 1, together with z_0^{pe_K(j−1)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz when j > 1 and p − 1 | e_K(j−1).
items.locator: Proposition 7.6 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 48–49
items.note: The refined algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequence is the truncation n ≥ je_K (resp. n − 1 ≥ (j − 1)e_K) of the refined algebraic Tate one. One class in the proof is misnamed (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 7.8: the kernel of can on E^2_{−1}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Leading terms refer to the refined algebraic spectral sequences; write the classes of E^2_{−1,2j} by their leading terms z_0^{n−1}σ^j dz. For j ≥ 1 the kernel of can : E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) → E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) is an e_K j-dimensional k-vector space with basis the cycles with leading terms z_0^{(pe_K(j−1)+bp^l)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz for l ≥ 0, p ∤ b, b ≡ −e_K(j−1) mod p − 1 and p^{l−1} ≤ e_K j/(pe_K − b) < p^l.
items.locator: Lemma 7.8 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 49–50

items.name: Lemmas 8.1–8.3: Frobenius on leading terms and on the refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. (1) For n ≥ e_K j, φ(z^nσ^j) = μ̄^{−pj}z^{p(n−e_K j)}σ^j. (2) If e_K > 1, φ(σ_0(z_0 − z_1)) ≡ −z_0^{p−1}σ_0(z_0 − z_1) mod 𝒩^{≥p/e_K+1}. (3) If α ∈ 𝒩^{≥m}TC^-_{2j}(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]; F_p), then φ(α) ∈ 𝒩^{≥p(m−j)}TP_{2j}(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]; F_p) (refined filtrations).
items.locator: Lemmas 8.1–8.3 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 50–51
items.note: (1) from Theorem 2.17(6): φ(E_K(z)σ) = φ(u) = σ; (2) from Lemma 6.19 and δ(E_K(z_0)) ≡ 1 mod (p, 𝒩^{≥p/e_K}); (3) from the divisibility of Lemma 3.14.

items.name: Proposition 8.4 and Corollary 8.5: the Frobenius on E^2_{−1}(TC^-(O_K); F_p)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For j ≥ 1, if α ∈ E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) is detected by z_0^{n−1}σ^j dz in the refined algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequence, then φ(α) ∈ E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) is detected by −μ̄^{−p(j−1)}z_0^{p(n−e_K(j−1))−1}σ^j dz in the refined algebraic Tate spectral sequence. Since n ↦ p(n − e_K(j−1)) matches the leading terms of Propositions 7.6 and 7.2 bijectively, φ : E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) → E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) is an isomorphism for j ≥ 1.
items.locator: Proposition 8.4, Corollary 8.5 and the proof of Proposition 8.4, arXiv v4 pp. 51–53
items.note: Direct for e_K > 3 from Lemmas 8.1–8.3; for e_K ≤ 3 by the tame base change T_m of Proposition 6.34 and Remark 6.38 (the footnote extends Lemma 6.36 to all rows j).

items.name: Corollary 8.6: Frobenius against the refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let α ∈ E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) have refined Nygaard filtration m. (1) For j ≥ 1 the filtration of φ(α) is p(m − j) + (p − 1)/e_K + 1, so it is > m, < m or = m according as m >, < or = (pj − 1)/(p − 1) − 1/e_K. (2) For j ≤ 0 the filtration of φ(α) is > m.
items.locator: Corollary 8.6 and proof, arXiv v4 p. 52
items.note: The proof's displayed formula writes a where j is meant (recorded under sourceIssues). Remark 8.17 draws the resulting three regions and the 'critical line' m − j = (j − 1)/(p − 1) − 1/e_K.

items.name: Lemma 8.7, Corollaries 8.8–8.9: can − φ on E^2_{−1}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. can induces a surjection E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) → 𝒩^{≥j}E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) for j > 0, an isomorphism for j ≤ 0, and surjections 𝒩^{≥m}E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-) → 𝒩^{≥m}E^2_{−1,2j}(TP) for m ≥ j. Hence can − φ : 𝒩^{≥m}E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) → 𝒩^{≥m}E^2_{−1,2j}(TP(O_K); F_p) is surjective for j ≥ 1 and m ≥ (pj − 1)/(p − 1), and can − φ is an isomorphism on E^2_{−1,2j} for j ≤ 0.
items.locator: Lemma 8.7, Corollaries 8.8–8.9, arXiv v4 pp. 53–54

items.name: Lemma 8.10: Hilbert 90 for k/F_p in additive form
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p with absolute Frobenius φ, and b ∈ k^×. The F_p-linear map bφ − id : k → k is bijective if N_{k/F_p}(b) ≠ 1; otherwise its kernel and cokernel are both isomorphic to F_p.
items.locator: Lemma 8.10, arXiv v4 p. 54
items.note: Stated without proof as 'a reformulation of Hilbert 90'. If N(b) = 1, multiplicative Hilbert 90 writes b = y/φ(y) with y ∈ k^×, and then bφ − id = y·(φ − id)·y^{−1}, whose kernel y·F_p and cokernel k/(φ − id)k ≅ F_p come from additive Hilbert 90; if bφ(α) = α with α ≠ 0 then b = α^{1−p} has norm 1. Mathlib has the multiplicative form for finite cyclic Galois extensions, groupCohomology.exists_div_of_norm_eq_one (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Hilbert90.lean:134), but not this deduction or the additive form.

items.name: The integer d and the class β
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let d be the least positive integer with p − 1 | e_K d and N_{k/F_p}(μ̄)^d = 1, and choose a (p − 1)-th root μ̄^{pd/(p−1)} of μ̄^{pd} in k (it exists by Lemma 8.10). β ∈ Ẽ^2_{0,0,2d}(TC(O_K); F_p) ⊆ E^2_{0,2d}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) is the class detected by μ̄^{pd/(p−1)}z^{pe_K d/(p−1)}σ^d.
items.locator: §8, paragraphs before Lemma 8.10 and Proposition 8.11, arXiv v4 p. 54

items.name: Propositions 8.11–8.12: the kernel and cokernel of can − φ in column 0
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Ẽ^2_{0,0,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) = F_p[β], and Ẽ^2_{0,1,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) is a free F_p[β]-module of rank 1; λ denotes an F_p-basis of Ẽ^2_{0,1,0}, so λ ∈ E^2_{−1,0}(TC(O_K); F_p).
items.locator: Propositions 8.11–8.12 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 54–55
items.note: E^2_{0,*}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) = k[z^{pe_K j_0/(p−1)}σ^{j_0}] with j_0 least such that p − 1 | e_K j_0, and φ acts on the generator by μ̄^{−pj_0} (Lemma 8.1), so Lemma 8.10 gives the kernel and cokernel. The paper says the proof of 8.12 follows by combining these.

items.name: Lemma 8.13 and Proposition 8.14: γ and the cokernel of can − φ in column −1
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. There is γ ∈ ker(can − φ) ⊆ E^2_{−1,2(d+1)}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) detected by μ̄^{pd/(p−1)}z^{pe_K d/(p−1)−1}σ^{d+1}dz, and Ẽ^2_{−1,1,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) is a free F_p[β]-module of rank 1 generated by can(γ) ∈ E^2_{−1,2(d+1)}(TP(O_K); F_p).
items.locator: Lemma 8.13, Proposition 8.14 and proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 54–55
items.note: γ is built from the leading term by Proposition 8.4 and corrected in higher filtration by Corollary 8.8; a class of the cokernel of highest leading term must sit on the critical line, where Lemma 8.10 applies.

items.name: Proposition 8.15: the kernel of can − φ in column −1 and the classes α^{(j)}_{i,l}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Ẽ^2_{−1,0,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) is a free F_p[β]-module with basis γ together with cycles detected by c z^{(pe_K(j−1)+bp^l)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz ∈ E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p), for l ≥ 0 and 0 < b < pe_K, p ∤ b, b ≡ −e_K(j−1) mod p − 1, p^{l−1} ≤ e_K j/(pe_K − b) < p^l, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, and c running over an F_p-basis of k. For 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K and 1 ≤ j ≤ d there is exactly one b ∈ [(p−1)i + 1, pi], hence one (b, l), satisfying these conditions; α^{(j)}_{i,l} (1 ≤ l ≤ f_K) denote the corresponding cycles, of bidegree (−1, 2j).
items.locator: Proposition 8.15 and proof, Remark 8.17 and the paragraph after it, arXiv v4 pp. 55–57
items.note: α ↦ α_1 identifies ker(can) with ker(can − φ) preserving leading terms, using α_2 = Σ_{i≥1}(can^{−1}φ)^i(α_1) where φ raises the filtration (Corollary 8.6).
